concepts.why: It correctly creates a new int array sized to the original, but it writes data2.length() instead of the field data2.length, a slip that would not compile.
It uses int correctly as the element type and the index type, with no reasoning about int rules.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The loop header and body are applied correctly to visit indices 0..length-1, but the bound uses length() instead of length.

concepts.quote: int[] copy = new int[data2.length()]; for (...) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: It applies the copy pattern (new array, then element-by-element copy) to data2, but writes length() instead of length; it gives no explanation of alias versus copy.
